notes: All risk-finding assertions pass in both configurations: the baseline finds the same problems. The skill's gain is entirely in structure (diagram, analogy, traced example, decisions, glossary).
Baseline was stronger on a clear verdict and concrete counter-asks (workflow: 'approve the plan, not this version'; contract: redline list). The skill has no instruction to give a go/no-go answer.
Skill runs take about 3.4x longer (394s vs 116s) and 35% more tokens. Pages are 50-60 KB vs 9-17 KB.
Both configurations pulled the user's personal memory into fictional test material. The skill should only use personal context the user brings up.
Contract with_skill rated auto-renewal low risk; defensible but worth a human look.
